note.subject: french
note.title: Present tense
note.overview: This lesson contains 52 enabled questions. It teaches Present tense through explicit translation, recall, grammar and application tasks.
learningGoals: Recall the core language for Present tense.
Identify the task direction before writing.
Explain errors by naming the article, subject, tense, auxiliary, agreement or negative rule.
Use the material in a short controlled sentence.
mustMemoriseRules: Identify the subject before choosing a present-tense ending.
aller, avoir and être are irregular and must be memorised.
Regular -er endings: e, es, e, ons, ez, ent.
Regular -ir endings: is, is, it, issons, issez, issent.
Regular -re endings: s, s, no ending, ons, ez, ent.
Negatives wrap around the finite verb.

questionInstructions.label: CONJUGATE
questionInstructions.whatToDo: Use the named subject/tense. The bare verb or correct subject + verb is accepted when stated.

questionInstructions.label: APPLY THE RULE
questionInstructions.whatToDo: Produce the exact item requested by the rule prompt.

questionInstructions.label: WRITE ALL FORMS
questionInstructions.whatToDo: Give every named form; reasonable order and separators are accepted.

workedExamples.prompt: Write the « je » form in the aller column.
workedExamples.why: The source conjugation table gives je → vais for aller. The subject decides the written ending.

workedExamples.prompt: Write the « tu » form in the aller column.
workedExamples.why: The source conjugation table gives tu → vas for aller. The subject decides the written ending.

workedExamples.prompt: Write the « il / elle / on » form in the aller column.
workedExamples.why: The source conjugation table gives il / elle / on → va for aller. The subject decides the written ending.

workedExamples.prompt: Write the « nous » form in the aller column.
workedExamples.why: The source conjugation table gives nous → allons for aller. The subject decides the written ending.

workedExamples.prompt: Write the « vous » form in the aller column.
workedExamples.why: The source conjugation table gives vous → allez for aller. The subject decides the written ending.

workedExamples.prompt: Write the « ils / elles » form in the aller column.
workedExamples.why: The source conjugation table gives ils / elles → vont for aller. The subject decides the written ending.

commonMistakes: Choosing an ending before identifying the subject.

quickCheck.question: Subject: tu
Subject: il / elle / on
Subject: nous
Subject: vous
Subject: ils / elles

beforeStartingPractice: Read every must-memorise rule.
Cover the answer column and retrieve at least six chunks.
Complete the 60-second self-check.
On each card, read the task label before the French/English stimulus.
note.markingReminder: Accents are displayed and corrected but not deducted. Base spelling, article, subject, verb form, auxiliary, agreement, negative order and required content are still marked.

note.subject: french
note.title: Passé composé
note.overview: This lesson contains 88 enabled questions. It teaches Passé composé through explicit translation, recall, grammar and application tasks.
learningGoals: Recall the core language for Passé composé.
Identify the task direction before writing.
Explain errors by naming the article, subject, tense, auxiliary, agreement or negative rule.
Use the material in a short controlled sentence.
mustMemoriseRules: Passé composé = present auxiliary + past participle.
Most activity verbs use avoir.
Movement verbs in the taught bank use être.
With être, add -e, -s or -es when required.
Time phrases such as hier and la semaine dernière signal completed past.
Some movement verbs use avoir when they take a direct object.

questionInstructions.label: CONJUGATE
questionInstructions.whatToDo: Use the named subject/tense. The bare verb or correct subject + verb is accepted when stated.

questionInstructions.label: APPLY THE RULE
questionInstructions.whatToDo: Produce the exact item requested by the rule prompt.

questionInstructions.label: TRANSLATE INTO FRENCH
questionInstructions.whatToDo: Translate the quoted English and write the complete French answer.

questionInstructions.label: TRANSLATE INTO ENGLISH
questionInstructions.whatToDo: Translate the quoted French and write the complete English meaning.

questionInstructions.label: COMPLETE THE FRENCH
questionInstructions.whatToDo: Do not translate the whole line; write only the word/chunk replacing _____.

note.title: Expanded past-participle bank
note.overview: This lesson contains 140 enabled questions. It teaches Expanded past-participle bank through explicit translation, recall, grammar and application tasks.
learningGoals: Recall the core language for Expanded past-participle bank.
Identify the task direction before writing.
Explain errors by naming the article, subject, tense, auxiliary, agreement or negative rule.
Use the material in a short controlled sentence.
mustMemoriseRules: Regular participles: -er→-é, -ir→-i, -re→-u often.
Learn irregular forms in families: prendre→pris, mettre→mis, voir→vu.
The past participle is not the same as a present-tense form.
A full passé composé still needs an auxiliary.
Accents are shown even though this app does not deduct them.

questionInstructions.label: CONJUGATE
questionInstructions.whatToDo: Use the named subject/tense. The bare verb or correct subject + verb is accepted when stated.

questionInstructions.label: TRANSLATE INTO FRENCH
questionInstructions.whatToDo: Translate the quoted English and write the complete French answer.

questionInstructions.label: TRANSLATE INTO ENGLISH
questionInstructions.whatToDo: Translate the quoted French and write the complete English meaning.

workedExamples.prompt: Give the past participle of « faire ».

workedExamples.prompt: Give the past participle of « dire ».

workedExamples.prompt: Give the past participle of « lire ».

workedExamples.prompt: Give the past participle of « écrire ».
workedExamples.why: The teacher coverage gives écrire → écrit (to write). In the passé composé, the past participle follows the correct auxiliary.

note.title: Model answers and sentence building
note.overview: This lesson contains 50 enabled questions. It teaches Model answers and sentence building through explicit translation, recall, grammar and application tasks.
learningGoals: Recall the core language for Model answers and sentence building.
Identify the task direction before writing.
Explain errors by naming the article, subject, tense, auxiliary, agreement or negative rule.
Use the material in a short controlled sentence.
mustMemoriseRules: Use the five-step recipe: time phrase, tense, detail, opinion/reason, link.
Keep one time frame controlled before mixing tenses.
Reuse accurate source chunks.
Present models describe habits; passé composé models report completed actions; futur proche models give plans.
Proofread articles, auxiliaries, agreement and negatives.

note.subject: french
note.title: Accuracy traps
note.overview: This lesson contains 50 enabled questions. It teaches Accuracy traps through explicit translation, recall, grammar and application tasks.
learningGoals: Recall the core language for Accuracy traps.
Identify the task direction before writing.
Explain errors by naming the article, subject, tense, auxiliary, agreement or negative rule.
Use the material in a short controlled sentence.
mustMemoriseRules: Correct the grammar job, not only the visible spelling.
Check opinion articles and negative articles separately.
Every passé composé verb needs the right auxiliary.
Être participles may agree with the subject.
Irregular participles must be recalled exactly.
Rewrite the whole corrected sentence.

questionInstructions.label: CORRECT THE ERROR
questionInstructions.whatToDo: Find the error and rewrite the whole corrected sentence.

questionInstructions.label: CHOOSE THE ANSWER
questionInstructions.whatToDo: Select exactly one option.

questionInstructions.label: COMPLETE THE FRENCH
questionInstructions.whatToDo: Do not translate the whole line; write only the word/chunk replacing _____.

questionInstructions.label: APPLY THE RULE
questionInstructions.whatToDo: Produce the exact item requested by the rule prompt.

workedExamples.prompt: Correct this: J’aime du pain.
workedExamples.why: After opinions, use the definite article.

workedExamples.prompt: Correct this: Je ne bois pas du coca.
workedExamples.answer: Je ne bois pas de coca.
workedExamples.why: After ne…pas, change to de / d’.

workedExamples.prompt: Correct this: J’ai allé au cinéma.
workedExamples.why: aller uses être.

workedExamples.prompt: Correct this: Elle a montée.
workedExamples.why: Movement verb → être.

workedExamples.prompt: Correct this: Nous sont arrivés.
workedExamples.why: nous takes sommes.

workedExamples.prompt: Correct this: Elles sont sorti.
workedExamples.why: Feminine plural agreement needed.

commonMistakes: Correcting only one word instead of rewriting the sentence.
Fixing spelling while leaving the grammar error.

learningGoals: Recall the core language for Master vocabulary.
Identify the task direction before writing.
Explain errors by naming the article, subject, tense, auxiliary, agreement or negative rule.
Use the material in a short controlled sentence.
mustMemoriseRules: Use the master bank for retrieval, not passive rereading.
Learn numbers in construction families.
Learn phrases as complete chunks with articles/prepositions.
Translate in both directions.
When a source row contains alternatives, the task must state whether one or all are required.

note.subject: french
note.title: KS3 extension irregular verbs
note.overview: This lesson contains 81 enabled questions. It teaches KS3 extension irregular verbs through explicit translation, recall, grammar and application tasks.
learningGoals: Recall the core language for KS3 extension irregular verbs.
Identify the task direction before writing.
Explain errors by naming the article, subject, tense, auxiliary, agreement or negative rule.
Use the material in a short controlled sentence.
mustMemoriseRules: The nine high-frequency verbs are irregular.
Learn all six subject forms, especially nous and ils/elles.
Faire, pouvoir, vouloir and devoir are frequent in speaking and writing.
Prendre, boire, lire, dire and venir support routine, school and food topics.
Do not add regular endings to an irregular stem.

mustMemoriseVocabulary.french: Je fais mes devoirs après le collège.
mustMemoriseVocabulary.english: I do my homework after school.

mustMemoriseVocabulary.french: Je peux aller au cinéma ce week-end.
mustMemoriseVocabulary.english: I can go to the cinema this weekend.
I want to buy a baguette.

mustMemoriseVocabulary.french: Je prends le petit déjeuner à sept heures.
mustMemoriseVocabulary.english: I have breakfast at seven o’clock.

mustMemoriseVocabulary.french: Je bois de l’eau, pas du coca.
Je lis un livre le soir.
mustMemoriseVocabulary.english: I read a book in the evening.
I say hello to the teacher.

note.title: Reflexives and routine
note.overview: This lesson contains 80 enabled questions. It teaches Reflexives and routine through explicit translation, recall, grammar and application tasks.
learningGoals: Recall the core language for Reflexives and routine.
Identify the task direction before writing.
Explain errors by naming the article, subject, tense, auxiliary, agreement or negative rule.
Use the material in a short controlled sentence.
mustMemoriseRules: Reflexive verbs need me/te/se/nous/vous/se.
Before a vowel, me/te/se shorten to m’/t’/s’.
Reflexive passé composé normally uses être.
Keep the reflexive pronoun before the auxiliary.
Add agreement where required.
